title: The AI-first repository framework: artifacts, concepts, rules, checks and rituals, and what binds them
note: Project-agnostic by construction: every node is a generic role, and 'seen' says in which of three repositories it exists today (H HogShade, L LargeWorlds, S SpriteJammer). Generated pages come from this file (tools/render_framework_graph.py); edit the data, not the pages.

layers.entry: What an agent reads first, and which file wins
layers.state: Where the project is right now, and who must decide what
layers.intent: What is about to be built, and the chain that gets it built
layers.decision: How decisions are taken, recorded and reviewed
layers.rule: The standing rules, the vocabulary and the failure ledger
layers.narrative: What happened, and which beliefs changed
layers.mechanics: The checks, templates, skills and reviews that make the rules bite

kinds.artifact: A file or directory that exists in the repository
kinds.concept: A named idea the framework uses
kinds.rule: A standing rule an agent must follow
kinds.check: Something that goes red when a rule is broken

relations.reads: A is read before or with B
relations.records: A holds a record of B
relations.gates: B may not proceed until A passes
relations.mechanises: A is the automatic check for rule B
relations.constrains: A bounds how B is written or used
relations.defines: A is where B is defined
relations.annotates: A is a mark carried by B

nodes.label: Entry file
nodes.summary: The tool-neutral map every agent reads first: golden rules and links to topic files; it carries no state.

nodes.label: Tool pointer files
nodes.summary: Thin per-tool files that import or point at the entry file and add only that tool's quirks.

nodes.label: Scoped instruction file
nodes.summary: A nested instruction file for one area (a package, a tool), subordinate to the entry file.

nodes.label: Documentation map
nodes.summary: A task-to-document table: if you are doing X, read Y in this order.

nodes.label: Reading order
nodes.summary: The entry file states what to read first, in order: the handoff, then the board, then the rest.

nodes.label: Pointer, not summary
nodes.summary: The entry file points and never states counts, phase or status, because a pointer does not go stale.

nodes.label: Canonical on conflict
nodes.summary: One file wins where two disagree on a fact; the other is a bug to fix.

nodes.label: Handoff
nodes.summary: The living snapshot a new session reads first: state, work in flight, and what the owner said that is written nowhere else.

nodes.label: Board
nodes.summary: The tracker: gates, now, next, blocked and the icebox. Status lives here and nowhere else.

nodes.label: Roadmap
nodes.summary: The tracks, phases and order of work; amended as decisions land; not the tracker.

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.summary: A decision only the owner can make; nothing downstream of an open gate may be committed to.

nodes.label: Icebox
nodes.summary: Where every idea said out loud lands, with a cost and a reason; an empty icebox means ideas are going missing.

nodes.label: Verdict on an idea
nodes.summary: A one-line judgement (awesome, good, meh) that orders an idea and never deletes it.

nodes.label: A mentioned feature is not a work order
nodes.summary: An idea goes on the board with a cost; it is built only when the owner says so, it blocks work in flight, or it is smaller than the conversation about it.

nodes.label: Landed row
nodes.summary: A finished board row is struck through and keeps its PR number; nothing is deleted.

nodes.label: Snapshot, not log
nodes.summary: The handoff states now; history belongs to the journal and to git, so the handoff never accretes sit reps.

nodes.label: Conversation-only context
nodes.summary: What the owner said that is written nowhere else (preferences, rejected options): recorded first in the handoff, or it is lost.

nodes.label: Where to be skeptical
nodes.summary: The handoff names the documents and claims known to be stale or soft, so a reader knows what not to trust.

nodes.label: Freeze a handoff
nodes.summary: Copy the handoff to a dated file and cut the live one to what is still true; used when a phase closes.

nodes.label: Lane-prefixed ids
nodes.summary: A session mints board ids only in its own lane, against the main branch, so two sessions never mint the same id.

nodes.label: Deferred bugs are issues
nodes.summary: The board tracks features, spikes and gates; a deferred defect is a tracker issue opened before the PR merges.

nodes.label: Pre-spec design
nodes.summary: The hand-written lock of the problem, the options and the decisions, written before any spec.

nodes.label: Spec
nodes.summary: One increment's exact deliverable, interfaces, acceptance gate and out-of-scope list.

nodes.label: Plan
nodes.summary: The ordered, checkbox tasks for one increment, each small enough to verify.

nodes.label: Increment
nodes.summary: One reviewable unit of work with its own spec, plan, pull request and close-out.

nodes.label: Design chain
nodes.summary: Converse and lock, design, spec, plan, test-first build; a board yes is not a lock.

nodes.label: Owner lock
nodes.summary: The owner's recorded yes that turns a design from exploring into accepted.

nodes.label: Who owns what
nodes.summary: Each record owns one thing (design: why; spec: what; plan: tasks; board: status; journal: narrative); duplication between them drifts.

nodes.label: Tick on verification
nodes.summary: A plan task is ticked when its verification ran, never when its code was written.

nodes.label: What the build found
nodes.summary: A section appended to a spec after the build, recording where reality differed from the plan.

nodes.label: Amendment after acceptance
nodes.summary: A change to a locked design is recorded in its own section with the owner's answer, never made silently.

nodes.label: Mock pass
nodes.summary: A generated UX canvas reviewed in its own pull request before the widget is built.

nodes.label: Spike
nodes.summary: Throwaway evidence code with the hypothesis written first; frozen, and never imported by production code.

nodes.label: Growth ladder
nodes.summary: Process is minimal now and grows with the codebase; no tier is added before its trigger.

nodes.label: ADR
nodes.summary: An append-only record of one structural decision, with its consequences and when to revisit it.

nodes.label: Decision log
nodes.summary: The index of every decision stated in conversation, with where it was formalised.

nodes.label: Supersede, do not rewrite
nodes.summary: An old decision is superseded by a new one with both ends stated; history is never edited.

nodes.label: Revisit if
nodes.summary: Every ADR names the condition under which it should be reopened; a decision with no expiry is a belief.

nodes.label: Two-way door
nodes.summary: A cheap-to-reverse decision: decide, record it, continue.

nodes.label: One-way door
nodes.summary: An expensive-to-reverse or owner-held decision: stop and ask.

nodes.label: Autonomy protocol
nodes.summary: Keep going until a real human decision is needed; decide the two-way doors and log them.

nodes.label: PR decisions table
nodes.summary: The PR section listing each two-way decision with its alternative, reason and cost to reverse.

nodes.label: Decision backstop
nodes.summary: More than eight logged decisions means split the PR or stop for review.

nodes.label: Pending-review queue
nodes.summary: A queue of two-way decisions made outside a PR, failing the build above a threshold.

nodes.label: The owner's merge is the review
nodes.summary: The assistant never merges; a decision not in the table was not reviewed.

nodes.label: Significant increment
nodes.summary: A change large or structural enough to earn the deliberate review (a new module or tool, a contract change, about 200 changed lines).

nodes.label: Standard
nodes.summary: A single-source topic file stating one family of rules, with the check that holds each.

nodes.label: Definition of done
nodes.summary: What ends an increment: the checks green and the repository's account of itself still true.

nodes.label: Failure-mode ledger
nodes.summary: Process defects as Trigger, Do, Because entries, appended in the same change as the fix.

nodes.label: Retrieval is enforcement
nodes.summary: A ledger works by being loaded before work starts; if it is not read it is a diary.

nodes.label: Mechanise the class
nodes.summary: Where a failure class can be caught by a check that goes red, build the check and link it from the entry.

nodes.label: Glossary
nodes.summary: The canonical vocabulary, one word per concept, with retired terms struck through and kept.

nodes.label: One word per concept
nodes.summary: No synonyms and no homonyms; a concept with two names is retrieved by neither.

nodes.label: Retired term
nodes.summary: A struck-through glossary row that the docs check forbids using as current.

nodes.label: Terms introduced
nodes.summary: A design, spec or plan names the glossary terms it introduces, or says None.

nodes.label: Grandfathered set
nodes.summary: The documents that predate a new rule; the set may shrink and never grow.

nodes.label: One rule, one home
nodes.summary: A rule has one canonical statement; other files link to it and never restate its rationale.

nodes.label: Status vocabulary
nodes.summary: A closed set of status words on governed documents; Proposed means a hypothesis, not a fact.

nodes.label: Claims after evidence
nodes.summary: Report done, passing or fixed only after the verification ran, and say what was not verified.

nodes.label: Prove the instrument
nodes.summary: A check is evidence only once it has produced the other answer; a control must fail.

nodes.label: A number needs its commit
nodes.summary: A measurement is quoted with the commit and machine it came from.

nodes.label: Say what was not covered
nodes.summary: Every pull request states what it left out and why.

nodes.label: Owner identity only
nodes.summary: Commits and pull requests carry the owner's identity; no AI attribution trailer.

nodes.label: Process ownership
nodes.summary: Never stop, or work on, a process or branch you did not start; another session may own it.

nodes.label: Hygiene
nodes.summary: No retired identifier, employer name or private path in tracked files; an allowlist names the exceptions.

nodes.label: Memory is not a record
nodes.summary: A session memory helps only a session that recalls it; durable facts go in the repository.

nodes.label: Journal
nodes.summary: The append-only narrative of what happened and which beliefs changed.

nodes.label: One file per day
nodes.summary: A new calendar day starts a new journal file and the session number restarts.

nodes.label: Beliefs that changed
nodes.summary: The most valuable journal content: what was believed, what contradicted it, what is true now.

nodes.label: Trailing arrow
nodes.summary: A closing line in a journal entry that links to the durable artifact the entry produced.

nodes.label: Parallel sessions
nodes.summary: Sessions running at once take the next number, link each other, and merge living documents by hand.

nodes.label: Devblog
nodes.summary: A weekly public human-story memo produced by a fresh-eyes pass chain, with a fail-closed privacy boundary.

nodes.label: Verification evidence
nodes.summary: Committed pictures and logs that plan tasks cite when they are ticked.

nodes.label: Picture rule
nodes.summary: Evidence pictures are bounded in size, fixed-named, overwritten in place and listed in a manifest.

nodes.label: Research note
nodes.summary: A lab-notebook entry: hypothesis written first, method, results, failures kept.

nodes.label: Review record
nodes.summary: A scored review pinned to a commit and never edited.

nodes.label: Knowledge file
nodes.summary: A small topic file rewritten as the topic settles, for an agent to load.

nodes.label: Generated document
nodes.summary: A document written by a tool from source data, committed, checked with --check, never hand-edited.

nodes.label: Docs check
nodes.summary: The drift checker: links, status lines, indexes, board shape, vocabulary, terms.

nodes.label: Hygiene check
nodes.summary: Fails on a retired identifier outside the allowlist.

nodes.label: Boundary test
nodes.summary: A stated dependency boundary has a test that fails when it is crossed.

nodes.label: Executable documentation
nodes.summary: A document's code block or generated page is run or regenerated by a test, so it cannot rot.

nodes.label: CI pipeline
nodes.summary: The merge gate: lint, docs check, hygiene, every generator's --check, the tests.

nodes.label: CI parity oracle
nodes.summary: The local check runner and CI are tested against one stage list, so green locally means green in CI.

nodes.label: Git hooks
nodes.summary: Pre-commit and commit-message hooks for the fast gate and the sign-off.

nodes.label: Branch-ownership tool
nodes.summary: Reports whether a branch or PR belongs to another live session; it can prove 'not yours' and almost never 'yours'.

nodes.label: Smoke gate
nodes.summary: Every application is launched and driven; any exception or blank frame fails.

nodes.label: PR template
nodes.summary: The close-out record: board line, what changed, verified, decisions, wrong along the way, review, not covered, checklist.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.summary: A plain-markdown procedure done twice, which an agent invokes.

nodes.label: Local review
nodes.summary: A fresh-eyes subagent scores the diff against the repository's standards and a rubric, 7 of 10 as the bar.

nodes.label: Automated review assessment
nodes.summary: Every automated review finding is verified against source, fixed or refuted with evidence, and answered on its thread.
